message.content: The company faces the risk that supply chain constraints will act as a governor on near-term revenue conversion, which would be confirmed if management states that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago or if they describe revenue conversion as likely to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. The company also faces the risk that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat, creating a high comparison bar for future profitability, which would be confirmed if management explicitly cautions that these impacts artificially pulled up 2026 profitability and will not recur [D3]. Additionally, the company risks that demand durability is questioned by analysts, which would be confirmed if investors press on whether demand is sustainable or if supply constraints are limiting guidance as seen in questions from Goldman Sachs and Truist during the earnings call [D3]. The risk that integration efforts are not fully complete would be confirmed if management indicated that systems migrations were delayed beyond one quarter ahead of schedule, though they stated integration efforts are largely complete including systems migrations one quarter ahead of schedule [D3]. Finally, the risk that the 6G opportunity is smaller than expected would be confirmed if management revised their base case to suggest the opportunity in 6G is not greater than the opportunity seen in 5G, contrary to their statement that they are well positioned to capitalize on it given the larger opportunity [D3].
